It was observed that in statement of computation of gross taxable income as well as determining deduction under section 80IA, assessee had added back above said finance cost (unwinding of interest cost) as above said finance cost was notional loss and therefore, was not allowable as deduction as revenue expenditure - Whether, therefore, impugned disallowance was to be deleted - Held, yes [Paras 31.2 and 31.5] [In favour of assessee] IV Section 37(1), read with section 43A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Business expenditure - Allowability Of (Forex loss) - Assessment year 2018-19 - Assessee had entered into contract with BHEL on turnkey basis for in-house development of a power plant - During course of execution of contract, BHEL had imported certain plant and machinery from abroad on account of which certain amount of consideration was payable by assessee in foreign currency - Assessing Officer had made an addition on account of foreign exchange loss incurred by assessee on payment of foreign exchange to BHEL as per contract for acquisition of capital asset from abroad treating same as capital expenditure - It was observed that assessee had reinstated forex liability in Balance Sheet and excess liability was claimed as forex loss - Further, foreign currency liability relating to above project remained with assessee till relevant liability was settled - Whether, therefore, impugned addition was to be deleted - Held, yes [Para 36.6] [In favour of assessee] V Section 32 of the Income-Tax Act, 1961 - Depreciation - Allowance/rate of (Power companies) - Assessment year 2018-19 - Assessee, engaged in electricity generation and distribution, claimed depreciation on fixed assets - Assessing Officer disallowed same by observing that assessee had not submitted working of depreciation - Commissioner (Appeals) sustained additions - It was observed that applicable rates as per section 32(1)(i) read with rule 5(IA) (Appendix 1A) were followed by assessee - Further, relevant depreciation schedule was submitted before Assessing Officer, which was part of audit report submitted as per Form 3CD - Whether, therefore, issue was to be remitted back to Assessing Officer to verify relevant depreciation schedule and also verify relevant documents submitted to claim that assets were already put to use on or before 31-3-2018 - Held, yes [Para 42] [Matter remanded]

Section 5  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual of - Assessment years 2004-05 and 2005-06 - Assessee-company was doing business in fields of hotel industries, resorts, clubs, etc. - It offered card facilities to its members, which included savings and discounts on purchases made by card members plus club facilities - It also offered holiday scheme to card members by way of advance sale of room nights to them at a discounted/special price - Members were entitled to utilize room nights as per terms of entitlement of scheme at any of hotels/clubs owned by assessee or its subsidiaries and also at other affiliated destinations - Further card members were entitled to surrender room nights in case they did not utilize them and might also opt for surrender value - In lieu of surrender value, members might also opt to buy or utilise products and services of assessee and its group companies - As per system of accounting adopted by assessee advance on sale of room nights was shown as an advance and thereafter income was apportioned based on happening of event of customer availing room nights - Assessing Officer passed assessment order accepting method of assessee - However, Commissioner, while exercising his powers under section 263 set aside assessment order on ground that entire advance received by assessee an account of sale of room night should have been taxed as income during year of receipt - Whether since amount received by assessee from its members on account of advance sale of room nights was a general amount wherein member had option of staying in many alternate properties as well as an option for refund of money with certain compensation called 'surrendered value' as well as an option to utilize/purchase products and services of assessee and its group companies, it could not be said that assessee had right to appropriate amount of advance on receipt, irrespective of rendering of service - Held, yes - Whether therefore, direction of Commissioner to tax entire amount received by assessee on account of advance sale of room nights as income during year was bad in law - Held, yes

I. Section 69B of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Undisclosed investments (Investment in immovable property) - Assessment years 2017-18 to 2019-20 - Assessee-company was involved in the business of running a hotel - A search was conducted in assessee's premises - Assessing Officer made additions under section 69C on account of difference in value of investment on construction of hotel building shown by assessee in books of account as compared to value of investment estimated by DVO in its report - Whether since no incriminating or corroborating evidence was found during course of search exhibiting unexplained investment by an assessee, impugned addition made by Assessing Officer purely on basis of DVO’s report which was a work of pure estimation of cost based on government rates was to be deleted - Held, yes [Paras 13 and 14] [In favour of assessee] II. Section 35AD of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Specified business, deduction in respect of expenditure on (Hotels) - Assessment years 2017-18 to 2019-20 - Whether section 35AD(5)(aa) nowhere mandates that date of certificate should be with effect from a particular date - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, where hotel being run by assessee had been duly granted a four star rating certificate by Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in subsequent assessment year, it would be eligible to claim deduction under section 35AD - Held, yes [Paras 34 and 37] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 69B of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Undisclosed investments (Investment in immovable property) - Assessment years 2017-18 to 2019-20 - Assessee-company was involved in the business of running a hotel - A search was conducted in assessee's premises - Assessing Officer made additions under section 69C on account of difference in value of investment on construction of hotel building shown by assessee in books of account as compared to value of investment estimated by DVO in its report - Whether since no incriminating or corroborating evidence was found during course of search exhibiting unexplained investment by an assessee, impugned addition made by Assessing Officer purely on basis of DVO’s report which was a work of pure estimation of cost based on government rates was to be deleted - Held, yes [Paras 13 and 14] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : Where during course of search, no incriminating material was found exhibiting unexplained investment in construction of hotel by assessee, addition made by Assessing Officer purely on basis of DVO’s report which was a work of pure estimation of cost based on government rates was to be deleted  INCOME TAX : Where hotel being run by assessee had been duly granted a four star rating certificate by Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in subsequent assessment year, it would be eligible of claim of deduction under section 35AD since provisions of section 35AD does not mandates that date of certificate should be with effect from a particular date

Section  56,  read with sections  147,148  and  149, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 /  Section  92 ,    read with  sections  279 ,   280   and   282   of the Income-tax Act, 2025 – Income from other sources – Chargeable as (Reassessment) - Assessment year  2017-18  - Assessee filed return declaring nil income – Based on DIT (I&CI) information regarding purchase of immovable property at value lower than stamp duty value, reassessment proceedings were initiated – Assessing Officer, pursuant to order under section 148A(d) and notice under section 148, invoked section 56(2)(vii)(b) and made addition of ?17.38 lakhs – Assessment was completed under section 143(3) read with section 147 – Whether since order under section 148A(d) and notice under section 148 were issued beyond limitation as per order of Apex Court in case of Union of India v. Rajeev Bansal [2024] 167 taxmann.com 70/301 Taxman 238/469 ITR 46 (SC), reassessment was time-barred and liable to be quashed – Held, yes [Para 9] [In favour of assessee]

Section 14A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 read with rule 8D of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 - Expenditure incurred in relation to income not includible in total income (Recording of Satisfaction) - Assessment year 2014-15 - Assessing Officer made an addition under section 14A read with rule 8D to assessee's income in respect of certain investment - On appeal, Tribunal deleted addition by holding that relevant investments were made using assessee's old and interest-free funds - In instant appeal, revenue contended that assessee had availed of mixed funds and utilized them for making investment into securities earning tax free income, and therefore, section 14A read with rule 8D would be attracted automatically - Whether condition precedent of recording requisite satisfaction which is a safeguard provided in section 14A should not be overlooked before going to rule 8 - Held, yes - Whether in such circumstances, submission canvassed on behalf of revenue that once there were mixed funds, rule 8 would be attracted automatically was not correct - Held, yes [Para 4.1] [In favour of assessee]  Section 14A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 read with rule 8D of the Income-tax rules, 1961 - Expenditure incurred in relation to income not includible in total income (Illustrations) - Assessment year 2014-15 - Assessing Officer made disallowance under section 14A read with rule 8D - Tribunal held that disallowance made under section 14A read with rule 8D could not exceed exempt income - Whether order of Tribunal was justified - Held, yes [Para 4.2] [In favour of assessee]  Section 115JB, read with section 14A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Minimum alternate tax - Payment of (Section 14A disallowance) - Assessment year 2014-15 - Assessing Officer made addition in book profit on basis of calculations worked out under section 14A - On appeal, Tribunal held that adjustment made on account of disallowance under section 14A, in computation of book profit under section 115 JB was not as per law - Whether no addition in book profit could be made on basis of calculations worked out under section 14A and therefore order of Tribunal was to be upheld - Held, yes [Para 4.3] [In favour of assessee]  Section 80-IA of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Deductions - Profits and gains from infrastructure undertakings (Computation of deduction) - Assessment year 2014-15 - Assessee had a CPP Unit generating electricity, which was supplying it to a general unit - Electricity generated was being supplied to other consumers also - CPP unit charged Rs. 5.40 ps. per unit from general unit - Assessing Officer applying sub-section (8) of section 80 IA restricted same to Rs. 5.32 ps. per unit and, thereby, restricted deductions claimed by assessee under section 80 IA - This restriction was primarily on basis that rate of Rs. 5.40 ps. charged by Gujarat Electricity Board ( GEB ) was inclusive of 8 paise per unit of electricity duty - This component of electricity duty Assessing Officer discarded for purposes of ascertaining market value of electricity generated by CPP Unit and supplied to its general unit - Tribunal, however, reversed orders passed by revenue authorities and held that market value of electricity supplied by CPP Unit to general unit would be same being charged by GEB from consumers and it ignored rate on which power generating company supplied its power to GEB - Whether order of Tribunal needed no interference - Held, yes [Para 4.4] [In favour of assessee]  Section 4 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Capital or revenue receipts (Carbon Credits) - Assessment year 2014-15 - Assessee earned income from trading of carbon credits - Assessing Officer treated same as revenue receipt - Tribunal however, held that assessee's income from trading of carbon credits should be in nature of capital receipts and therefore, would not invite tax - Whether order of Tribunal needed no interference - Held, yes [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 5 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual of [Membership fee] - Assessment year 2006-07 - Assessee was engaged in business of running holiday homes on time share basis - It provided holiday home facility to its members for a period of 25 years - In a 25 years plan, 60 per cent membership fees was treated as income of assessee of first year and balance 40 per cent was treated as income of remaining 24 years on a pro rata basis - Assessing Officer treated hundred per cent of membership collection as income liable for taxation for impugned assessment year - Whether in view of Special Bench decision in Asstt. CIT v. Mahindra Holiday  Resorts (India) Ltd. [2010] 39 SOT 438 (Chennai - Trib.) assessee was justified in treating only 60 per cent of its membership fee collection as its income of impugned assessment year - Held, yes [Para 24] [In favour of assessee]IT : Assessee engaged in business of running holiday homes on time share basis was justified in treating only 60 per cent of its membership fee collection as its income of impugned assessment year   IT : Expenditure incurred for procuring furniture during construction would be capital expenditure   IT : Licence fee paid for using software for period of three years would be revenue expenditure   IT : Market research expenses for launching new project would be capital expenditure even if said project did not take place

Section  5,  read with section  145,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961/ Section  5,  read with section  276,  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 -  Income  -  Accrual of  (Time-share membership fee) - Assessment years 1998-1999 to 2002-2003 - Assessee-company, engaged in time-share business, collected membership fee upfront for 33 years and credited portion to Deferred Income account, recognising 40 per cent as income in initial years and 60 per cent in later years, deferring balance over contract period - Assessing Officer disallowed deferral, citing mercantile system and lack of provision to defer revenue, and noted separate collection of annual maintenance and utility charges - Whether, in view of judicial precedents, time-share membership fee received upfront could be deferred and recognised as income over tenure of membership contract, applying matching principle, notwithstanding mercantile system and absence of express statutory provision to defer revenue, and despite separate collection of annual maintenance and utility charges - Held, yes [Paras 15 and 16] [In favour of assessee]

Section 56, read with section 263, of the Income-tax Act, 1961, read with rules 11UA and 11U of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 - Income from other sources - Chargeable as (Share premium) - Assessment year 2016-17 - Assessee-company issued shares for Rs. 1087 per share at premium of Rs. 987 - Principal Commissioner opined that as per rule 11U and 11UA fair market value of shares was computed at Rs. 450 per share - He, thus invoked revisionary proceedings and set aside assessment order on ground that Assessing Officer failed to assess share premium received over and above fair market value of Rs. 450 by applying provisions of section 56(2)(viib) - It was noted that assessee submitted valuation report wherein DCF method was used to determine value of shares whereas Principal Commissioner utilised NAV method to determine FMV - Whether valuation method opted by assessee could not be changed in view of statutory mandate of rule 11UA(2) and, thus, action of Principal Commissioner was in direct contravention to provisions of Explanation (a)(i) to section 56(2)(viib) read with rule 11UA - Held, yes - Whether thus, revisionary order was to be quashed - Held, yes [Paras 45 and 46] [In favour of assessee]  Section 4, read with sections 199 and 263, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 and rule 37BA of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 - Income - Assessable as (Revision) - Assessment year 2016-17 - Assessee-company imported machinery for construction of its hotel - For importing said machinery EPCG licenses were availed and fixed deposits were required to be made for obtaining bank guarantee against EPCG licenses - Assessee received interest income on said fixed deposits and claimed TDS on said interest income in its return - Principal Commissioner invoked revisionary proceedings on ground that assessee claimed TDS on interest income, however no such income was offered for taxation and amount was not assessed correctly by Assessing Officer - Whether since fixed deposits and interest received were directly linked with activity of setting up hotel, said interest was to be viewed as a capital receipt going to reduce cost of construction - Held, yes - Whether thus, view taken by Assessing Officer was a plausible view and revisionary order was to be quashed - Held yes [Paras 60 and 62] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars and Notifications : Instruction no. 173/14/2018-ITAT, dated 6-2-2018

Section 34(3), read with section 28(1)(c), of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 [corresponding to section 153(2)(b), read with section 271(1)(c), of the income-tax act, 1961]-Assessment-Time limit for completion-Assesses filed loss return for assessment year 1953-54 but ITO completed assessment on 27-3-1962 at income of Rs. 99,980 after making certain additions/ disallowances and recording satisfaction as to applicability of section 28(1)(c)-AAC annulled assessment, being time barred and not covered by extended time-limit of eight years under section 34(3) read with section 28(1)(c)-Tribunal sustained impugned assessment observing that there was material on record for ITO's satisfaction about applicability of section 28(1)(c)-Whether it was incumbent upon tribunal to dec1db on its own question of applicability of section 28(1)(c) for deciding the question of time limit-Held, yes-Whether extended time limit of eight years was available in present case-Held, case remanded to tribunal for first deciding question of applicability of section 28(1)(c)

Section 73, read with section 67 of Finance Act, 1994 - Recovery of service tax not levied or paid or short-levied or short-paid or erroneously refunded - Period from 16-7-2001 to 31-3-2005 - Assessee did not include value of material used in providing photography service in taxable value of service - Revenue invoking extended period of limitation demanded service tax from assessee - Tribunal in CCE v. Satyam Digital Photo Lab [2012] 34 STT 56/[2011] 16 taxmann.com 220 (New Delhi-Cestat) and CCE v. R.K. Photo Studio vide [Final Order Nos. ST/503-504/2011 dated 25-8-2011] held that extended period of limitation would not stand for demanding tax on this issue during relevant period - HELD: in view of above decision, demand was time-barred [Para 3] [In favour of assessee] Circulars & Notifications : Boards Circular F. No. 233/2/2003-CX dated, 7-4-2004

Section 149 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 [Corresponding to section 34 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922] - Income escaping assessment - Time-limit for issuance of notice - Assessment year 1939-40 - Whether where a person has been paid and he has accepted payment as interest no book-keeping can ever alter nature of that payment - Held, yes - Assessee carried on moneylending business and also owned certain zamindari property - He had purchased interest of mortgagee in 1920 in execution of decree obtained against mortgagee by assessee's father - In 1922 he instituted a suit on mortgage - Subsequently, he received certain amounts as interest on mortgage - Said amounts were, however, not included in his returns as litigation was pending - Department was also of opinion that assessee had treated all payments as being made into a suspense account - Upto 1930, assessee received all payments as interest - ITO sought to re-assess assessee under section 34 of 1922 Act in respect of said payments as income of year 1939-40 when money decree was satisfied by debtor by handing over another property to decree holder - Whether since payments had been received by assessee as interest their nature could not changed by treating them as being payments into suspense account - Held, yes - Whether payments were received by assessee as income before eight years of assessment under section 34 of 1922 Act, therefore, assessment of amounts in question in relevant assessment year was illegal - Held, yes

II. Section 5 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual of (Club membership fee) - Assessee-club collected non-refundable deposits from its members which was operational for a period of 10 years with a rider that liability attached to pay membership fee was for 10 years - Whether fee was to be spread over a period of 10 years and whole amount could not be taxed in year of receipt - Held, yes [Para 8][In favour of assessee]

Section  48  of the Income-tax Act, 1961/  Section  72   of the Income-tax Act, 2025 - Capital gains – Computation of (Indexation of cost of acquisition) - Assessment year  2015-16  - Assessee, an individual (non-resident), purchased an under-construction flat for Rs. 22 lakhs via an agreement executed and registered in March 2002, claiming indexation of entire cost from financial year 2001-02 - However, Assessing Officer (AO) recomputed indexed cost by applying indexation only to years of actual instalment payments, resulting in a disallowance of Rs. 2.43 lakhs under 'Capital Gains' - Whether indexation should be computed from year of acquisition of rights (i.e., allotment/registration) and not based on actual payment years - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, Assessing Officer was to be directed to delete addition made by him - Held, yes [Paras 12 and 12.1] [In favour of assessee]

III. Section  4  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Income  -  Chargeable as  (Deferred income) - Assessment year  2018-19  - Assessee-company was engaged in business of running resorts and hotels - It had devised concept of time shares wherein a person acquiring membership of such time share was assured of stay facility in resorts/hotels over period of membership - It followed a consistent accounting policy of recognizing a portion of time-share membership fee receipts as income in year of receipt and deferring balance to be recognized over tenure of services - Assessing Officer was of view that entire amount should be taxed in year of receipt and added deferred income to assessee's taxable income - Whether, on facts, since identical issue had already been decided by Tribunal in assessee's own case for earlier assessment years, following same, impugned addition made by Assessing Officer was to be deleted - Held, yes [Paras 19 and 20] [In favour of assessee]

Section 32, read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Depreciation - Unabsorbed depreciation (Period of carry forward) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessment was sought to be reopened on ground that allowance of set-off of brought forward unabsorbed depreciation pertaining to assessment years 1984-85 to 2007-08 being beyond 8 years was irregular - On similar issue in General Motors India (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2013] 354 ITR 244/[2012] 25 taxmann.com 364/210 Taxman 20 (Mag.) (Guj), High Court had held that unabsorbed depreciation could be allowed to be carried forward and set off without any reference to time limit - Whether on such basis, notice for reopening was to be quashed - Held, yes [Para 12] [In favour of assessee]IT : Reassessment deprecated as Court held that unabsorbed depreciation could be allowed to be carried forward and set off without any reference to time limit

IV. Section  5  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / Section  5  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 – Income -  Accrual of (Deferred income)  - Assessment year  2015-16  - Assessee-company, engaged in selling vacation home and leisure hospitality services, filed loss return - AO made addition on account of deferred income by rejecting assessee’s method of recognizing income in part over period of entitlement and did not follow Tribunal’s orders in assessee’s own earlier years, citing pendency of revenue’s appeal before High Court - CIT(A) deleted addition, observing that Tribunal’s orders in assessee’s own case remained valid in absence of any stay or reversal by a higher court and, following those orders, accepted assessee’s method of income recognition - Whether since revenue did not controvert facts relied by assessee, no infirmity was found in appellate order, and same was upheld - Held, yes [Paras 19 and 20] [In favour of assessee]

Section  28(i),  read with section  145,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961/Section  26,  read with section  276,  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 -  Business income  -  Chargeable as  (Recognition of income) - Assessment years  1997-98 to 2001-02  - Assessee-company, engaged in time-share business, operated membership scheme granting resort usage rights for 99 years - Assessee recognized 45 per cent of membership consideration as income in year of receipt and treated balance 55 per cent as advance subscription towards customer facilities, shown on liability side, to meet future obligations relating to amenities and facilities during balance membership period - Assessing Officer, while completing scrutiny assessment for A.Y. 1997-98, held that advance subscription could not be treated as deferred income and brought deferred 55 per cent portion to tax in year of receipt - Similar additions were made for remaining assessment years - Tribunal upheld additions holding that concept of deferred income was alien to Income-tax Act - Whether deferred income, matching principle and proportionate completion method are recognized concepts under Income-tax Act and revenue from continuing service obligations can be recognized on time basis - Held, yes - Whether since assessee had continuing obligation to maintain and provide facilities to members throughout 99-year membership period, entire membership fee could not be treated as income of first year itself - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, assessee’s method of deferring part of membership income to match future expenditure obligations was allowable - Held, yes [Paras 16, 17 and 19] [In favour of assessee]

Section 217 of Income-tax Act, 1961
Abdul Majid v. ITO [1991] 39 TTJ (Delhi) 154
Where assessment was made for the first time on 17-4-1986 under section 148, the Assessing Officer was justified in charging interest under section 139(8)/217 as per the law as it existed after amendment with effect from 1-4-1985.

Section  5,  read with section  145,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / Section  5,  read with section  276,  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 -  Income  -  Accrual of  (Recognition of income) - Assessment year  2002-03  - Assessee-company operated timeshare resorts and collected membership fee upfront at time of enrolment - It recognised 45 per cent of fee as income of current year and deferred balance 55 per cent to be spread over term of contract - Assessing Officer held that under mercantile system entire income had accrued in current year and disallowed deferment - Tribunal held that entire upfront fee was not taxable in initial year in view of assessee’s continuing contractual obligation to provide services over term of contract - It was noted that in case similar to assessee, Tribunal held that membership fee was a revenue receipt, yet it could not be brought to tax in one year and should be recognized on a rational or time basis in light of Accounting Standard 9 - Furthermore, said view had received seal of approval of Supreme Court - Whether thus, impugned order passed by Tribunal was to be upheld - Held, yes [Para 12] [In favour of assessee]

Section  5,  read with section  145,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961/ Section  5  read with section  276  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 -  Income  -  Accrual of  (Upfront time-share membership fee) - Assessment year  2003-04  - Assessee-company, engaged in time-share business, enrolled members on payment of membership fees upfront or in instalments, granting right to occupy and use resort facilities for specified days every year over membership tenure of 25/33 years - Assessee recognised 60 per cent of membership fee as income of year and deferred balance 40 per cent over contract period - Annual Maintenance Charges and utility charges were collected separately from members - Assessing Officer held that entire membership fee received was taxable in year of receipt - Commissioner (Appeals) and Tribunal accepted method of accounting followed by assessee - Whether since membership fees collected were coupled with continuing obligations extending till end of agreement period and were not merely entrance fees but also consideration for assured accommodation and allied facilities over membership tenure, deferment of part of membership fee over contract period was justified and entire receipt could not be taxed in year of receipt - Held, yes [Paras 10, 11 and 21] [In favour of assessee]

Sections 246-251 of Income-tax Act, 1961
Appeal against levy of interest under section 139(8) on ground of limitation is maintainable
Raj Auto & Diesel Service v. ITO [1993] 45 TTJ (Bang.) 178
Appeal against levy of interest under section 139(8) on ground of limitation is maintainable.

Section 5 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual of - Assessment years 1995-96 to 1998-99 - Assessee was engaged in business of hoteliering and setting up of resorts of different tourist destinations - It was undertaking two commercial activities in hotels - First activity was selling rooms to drive in guests for shorter or longer duration - Second activity was selling rooms to customers for a span of years to be availed by customers concurrently under a fixed pre-paid consolidated selling price - Second activity was popularly known as time share scheme in which each unit sold to customers was called a time share unit and comprised of fixed period of 99 years - Assessee used to collect lump sum amount from these customers purchasing a unit of time share - Assessee treated 45 per cent portion as income of year of receipt on account of sale of time share unit, whereas 55 per cent portion was transferred to reserve account and reckoned as a deferred revenue income and 1/99th of same was credited to profit and loss account each year - Whether, revisional authority was right in bringing to tax 100 per cent of assessee’s receipt on account of time share sale - Held, no

Section 7 of Wealth-tax Act, 1957
In case of let out property rent capitalisation method is the appropriate method for determining value of property and reversionary value of land should not be separately added to valuation arrived at by applying the provisions of Schedule III
Sanghi Brothers (Indore) Ltd. v. Dy. CWT [1995] 52 TTJ (Indore) 700
In case of let out property the rent capitalisation method which has been given recognition in Schedule III would be the appropriate method for determining the value of the property and reversionary value of land should not be separately added to the valuation arrived at by applying the provisions of Schedule III.

Section 5 of Income-tax Act, 1961
Where the assessee, a cement manufacturer, got a sum by way of relief on price escalation based on coal consumption of wet process plants for the assessment year 1983-84 as a result of a High Court decision but SLP against High Court decision was dismissed only on 13-4-1985 (assessment year 1986-87), such relief amount was assessable as assessee’s income in assessment year 1986-87 and not in assessment year 1983-84
Associated Cement Cos. Ltd. v. Inspecting Assistant Commissioner [1994] 49 TTJ (Bom.) 623
Where the assessee, a cement manufacturer, got a sum by way of relief on price escalation based on coal consumption of wet process plants for the assessment year 1983-84 as a result of a High Court decision but SLP against High Court decision was dismissed only on 13-4-1985 (assessment year 1986-87) such relief amount was assessable as the assessee’s income in the assessment year 1986-87, and not in the assessment year 1983-84.

Section 5  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual of (Contributions) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Where assessee company was set up for enabling members to discharge their effluents to be used for several years, capital contribution received from members could not be assessed in year of receipt but same to be spread over a period of five years [In favour of assessee]

Section 5  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual of - Assessment years 1998-99 to 2002-03 - Whether interest on enhanced compensation would not accrue till issue of enhanced compensation is finally decided and thereafter, on attaining finality of determination of enhanced compensation by Court, interest accrued to assessee has to be spread over on an annual basis right from date of delivery of possession till date of order of Court on time basis - Held, yes

Sections 150 & 153 of Income-tax Act, 1961
Levy of interest under sections 139(8) and 215 is part of assessment and thus limitation prescribed under section 153(1)(a)(iii)/153(2A) is applicable to order passed pursuant to appellate order for levy of interest
Raj Auto & Diesel Service v. ITO [1993] 45 TTJ (Bang.) 178
Levy of interest under sections 139(8) and 215 is part of assessment and thus limitation prescribed under section 153(1)(a)(iii)/153(2A) is applicable to order passed pursuant to appellate order for levy of interest.

Section 2(e), read with section 17A of the Wealth-tax Act, 1957 - Assets - Assessment years 1957-58 to 1959-60 - Assessee company entered into some settlement with Investigation Commission in respect of concealed income - Amount settled was not shown by assessee in its original return WTO initiated proceedings under section 17 and included that amount in net wealth of assessee - Tribunal found that assessee company did not have any secret funds or assets representing said concealed income on relevant valuation date and that directors had taken and utilised entire secret income and that no amount was brought into company’s books of account - Accordingly, Tribunal deleted addition - It was found that company itself never advanced any money to directors as a loan and it never had any access to these amounts - Further, statement which Investigation Commission submitted was in relation to assessment years 1940-41 to 1947-48 and wealth-tax was assessed nearly more than ten years after said event and there was no acknowledgment by anyone to extend period of limitation - Whether so called debts, viz., amounts in question became time-barred long before and hence, it could not be said that on valuation date those amounts represented assets of company - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, Tribunal was justified in deleting said amount - Held, yes

Section 65(82), read with sections 67 and 73, of the Finance Act, 1994 - Port services - Stay Order - Period from 1-4-2004 to 31-3-2007 - Assessee was a provider of port service - Assessee entered into agreement with M/s. GAC for construction of two captive jetty - Cost of construction was to be initially borne by M/s. GAC and expenditure incurred for construction was to be adjusted against wharfage charges by way of rebate/concession till capital cost was recovered - Assessee also collected lease rent for water front charges and leave way facility compensation - Department sought service tax on such rebate/concession and lease rent alleging deflation of value by assessee and invoked extended period of limitation - Held : On similar issue in case of very same assessee, Tribunal had granted relief as reported in Gujarat Maritime Board v. CCE [2011] 31 STT 89 (Ahd. - CESTAT) (Mag.) - Further, since similar issue had to be referred to Larger Bench, it would show that two views were possible - Revenue's allegation that there was suppression of facts only on the ground that agreement was drafted in a complicated manner with intention to evade payment of service tax was rejected, as no evidence of suppression was forthcoming and such agreement had been entered into before liability of Service Tax arose - Hence, prima facie, extended period of limitation was not invocable - Pre-deposit of Rs. 25 lakh was ordered [Para 15] [In favour of assessee] [Majority per : Ms. Archana Wadhwa, Judicial Member and B.S.V. Murthy, Member (TM)]ST : When similar issue had to be referred to Larger Bench, it would show that two views were possible and, therefore, prima facie, extended period of limitation cannot be invoked

I. Section  43CA  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / Section  53  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 – Full value of consideration for transfer of assets other than capital assets in certain case (Scope of provision) - Assessment year  2014-15  - Assessee, a real estate developer, sold two flats in its project for a combined stated consideration of Rs. 2.42 crores - Booking/allotment and receipt of consideration occurred in FY 2011-12, but agreements were registered in AY 2014-15 - Assessing Officer invoked section 43CA and substituted stamp duty value of Rs. 4.48 crores for stated consideration, resulting in addition of Rs. 2.06 crores - It was noted that flats were allotted and agreements were duly executed during A.Y. 2012-13 itself - Whether rigours of section 43CA, inserted with effect from 01.04.2014, would not be applicable to impugned transactions - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, addition made by Assessing Officer was unsustainable in law and liable to be deleted - Held, yes [Para 8] [In favour of assessee]

Section 139(8), read with sections 217 and 154 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Return of income - Interest for late filing of - Assessment years 1978-79 to 1980-81 - Whether interest under sections 139(8) and 217 can be charged at time of rectification of assessment order - Held, yes

I Section 5, read with section 145, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual Of (Time of accrual - Late payment surcharge) - Assessment year 2018-19 - Assessee was engaged in business of generation of electricity and distributed same through intermediaries - It had entered into Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with DISCOMS to regulate terms and conditions in respect of sale of power - Based on PPAs, assessee was eligible to claim sale prices of electricity and late payment surcharge (LPSC) of existing rate of 1.5 per cent per month in case sale considerations were settled beyond agreed period of settlement - Assessing Officer had made an addition of LPSC as income of assessee on ground that assessee followed mercantile system of accounting and same was chargeable to tax whether it was received or receivable - Whether as per accounting standard and norms, assessee had to declare its income not only based on accrual system but also supported by concept of certainty of recovery - Held, yes - Whether since assessee had not recovered any LPSC in past, impugned addition was to be deleted - Held, yes [Para 20] [In favour of assessee]INCOME TAX : Where assessee was engaged in distribution of electricity and Assessing Officer had made addition of late payment surcharge (LPSC) on overdues as income of assessee, since assessee had not recovered any LPSC in past, impugned addition was to be deleted  INCOME TAX : Where Assessing Officer had made an addition on account of interest expenditure relatable to amount invested by assessee in in-house development of project, since project was commissioned in financial year 2013-14 and interest was already determined and capitalized at time of commissioning of project itself, impugned addition was unsustainable  INCOME TAX : Where unwinding of interest on vendor liabilities being a notional loss charged as finance cost in books of accounts was added back for purpose of deduction under section 80IA(4)(iv) as same was not allowable as revenue expenditure, disallowance of same made by Assessing Officer under section 80IA(4) was to be deleted  INCOME TAX : Foreign exchange loss incurred by assessee on payment of foreign exchange to BHEL as per contract for acquisition of capital asset from abroad was allowable under section 37(1)  INCOME TAX : Where Assessing Officer disallowed depreciation claimed by assessee on fixed assets by observing that assessee had not submitted working of depreciation, since assessee had submitted relevant depreciation schedule before Assessing Officer which was part of audit report submitted as per Form 3CD, issue was to be remitted back to Assessing Officer to verify same

Section 28(i), read with section 254, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Business income - Year in which chargeable (On money) - Assessment years 1987-88 and 1988-89 - During 8 years period of 1980-81 to 1987-88, assessee-builder entered into agreements for sale of flats in its project for Rs. 3.77 crore - During search, 'on-money' of Rs. 66 lakhs was found to be charged by assessee over and above Rs. 3.77 crore - On-money of Rs. 26 lakhs and Rs. 40 lakhs was offered for taxation in assessment years 1987-88 and 1988-89 following project completion method of accounting and on basis that project was substantially completed during last two years - Assessing Officer assessed total 'on-money' at a normative figure by dividing it over 8 years - Total on-money for project was worked out to be Rs. 1,25,78,000 - Whether revenue could not bring to tax amount of Rs. 26 lakhs and Rs. 40 lakhs again in assessment years 1987-88 and 1988-89 - Held, yes [Paras 9 to 11] [Partly in favour of assessee]IT: Where on-money charged over and above cost of flats were shown by assessee builder in last two years when project was substantially completed while Revenue spread it over 8 years duration of projects, on-money amount shown in last 2 years was to be excluded

Section 69 of the Income-tax Act, 1961
Where total amount taken by Department to have been invested in construction of hotel came to Rs. 32 lakhs and odd as against cost of construction, valued by DVO, at Rs. 25.30 lakhs, total investment could not be taken at a figure higher than that determined by DVO [Assessment year 1993-94] [In favour of assessee]
CIT v. Pokar Hotel [2009] 226 CTR (Raj.) 101
The assessee’s income could not be assessed, under the head of investment, in construction of building, in an amount, beyond what was shown to be the cost, by the DVO, on the ground, that the assessee has shown investment, to be at lesser figure.
Thus, where though the DVO had determined the cost of construction of the hotel building at Rs. 25.30 lakhs, the total amount taken by the department to have been invested in the construction of hotel came to Rs. 32 lakhs and odd, as declared by assessee, inclusion of the amount of investment, in the construction of building, in an amount beyond what was shown to be the cost by the DVO, could not be sustained.

Section  149,  read with sections  148,  153A  and  153C, of the Income-tax Act, 1961/  Section  282   read with  section  280   of the Income-tax Act, 2025 -  Income escaping assessment  -  Time limit for issuance of notice (Illustrations)  - Assessment year  2015-16  - Assessee-company filed return for assessment year 2015-16 - On 28.03.2025, Assessing Officer issued notice under section 148 to reopen assessment year 2015-16, based on a search under section 132 conducted in financial year 2024-25 that allegedly revealed accommodation purchase entries indicating escapement of income - Whether while computing extended ten-year period under Explanation 1 to Section 153A read with section 153C, assessment year relevant to previous year of search is to be included in reckoning - Held, yes - Whether since search was conducted on 18.05.2024, impugned notice under section 148 dated 28.03.2025 for assessment year 2015-16 was barred by limitation as same fell beyond permissible period of ten years - Held, yes [Paras 9 and 10] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 80-IB, read with sections 139(1) and 153A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Deductions - Profits and gains from industrial undertaking other than infrastructure development undertakings (Enhanced claim) - Assessment years 2005-06 to 2010-11 - Whether where deduction claimed under section 80-IB in return under section 139(1) was increased while filing return in response to notice under section 153A and such enhancement was on account of arithmetical mistake and Assessing Officer had not pointed out any mistake in enhancement claim or had not brought out anything contrary to claim, except pointing out fact that claim had been enhanced, assessee would be entitled to enhanced claim under section 80-IB - Held, yes [Paras 12, 14 and 15] [In favour of assessee]  II. Section 32 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Depreciation - Additional depreciation (Windmills) - Assessment years 2006-07, 2008-09 and 2010-11 - Whether additional depreciation on windmills acquired and installed prior to 31-3-2002 is available under section 32(l)(iia) - Held, yes - Whether all that is required for allowing additional depreciation is that assessee must be engaged in manufacture or production of any article or thing, and such an assessee on setting up of a new machinery or plant would be entitled to additional depreciation on new plant or machinery under section 32(l)(iia) - Held, yes - Whether there is no requirement in section 32(1) (iia) that additional depreciation on new plant or machinery would be available only if plant or machinery has some nexus/connection with article or thing being manufactured by assessee - Held, yes [Para 21] [In favour of assessee]  III. Section 37(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Business expenditure - Allowability of (Compounding fees) - Assessment years 2005-06 and 2006-07 - Assessing Officer on perusal of audit report observed that assessee incurred expenditure for overloading of trucks - Assessee submitted before Assessing Officer that amount so paid was not in violation of law but an option given to assessee to pay compounding fees for transportation over dimensional consignments generally termed as overloading charges and expenses were not penalty in nature and not infringement of law - Assessing Officer did not accept plea of assessee and disallowed assessee's claim holding that said expenditure was in nature of penalty for violation of law and thus, not allowable - However it was found that expenditure incurred by assessee was compounding fee, charged by RTO for overloading trucks which was necessary for smooth functioning of business of assessee - Whether, therefore, deduction would be allowable - Held, yes [Para 28] [In favour of assessee]  IV. Section 69A, read with section 147, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Unexplained moneys (Cash paid for interior works) - Assessment year 2008-09 - During search proceedings at office premises of RBSS, certain loose papers were seized which had some details related to payments made to ED Architects in respect to interior work done at two houses of assessee - Assessee was unable to explain this entry and it was presumed by Assessing Officer that contents of document seized were true and therefore an amount of Rs. 15 lakhs was added to total income of assessee as undisclosed income - On appeal, Commissioner (Appeals) deleted addition - It was observed that, this issue was not explained by assessee during assessment proceedings before Assessing Officer, however, before Commissioner (Appeals) assessee had pointed out from ledger account that Rs. 15 lakhs had been paid by cheque to W and impugned entry of Rs. 15 lakhs was same and duly accounted in books of account - Whether therefore, addition made by Assessing Officer had rightly been deleted - Held, yes [Para 33] [In favour of assessee]  V. Section 23, read with section 22, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income from house property - Annual value (Computation of) - Assessment year 2010-11 - Assessee purchased a flat on 26-6-2009 - Assessing Officer found that assessee failed to offer annual value as per section 22 on property which was other than self-occupied property and accordingly made addition on account of income from house property - However, flat was not habitable on date of sale deed - There were further improvements in property - Certificate dated 12-8-2010 had been issued by Architect for completion of work and it was completed on 30-9-2010 - Whether therefore, no annual letting value (ALV) could be determined in such circumstances under section 23(1)(a) for year under consideration - Held, yes - Whether therefore, disallowance made by Assessing Officer was not in accordance with law and was directed to be deleted - Held, yes[Para 38] [In favour of assessee]

Section 139(8), read with section 217, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Return of income - Interest for late filing of - Assessment years 1982-83 to 1984-85 - For relevant years assessees were having income below taxable limit and hence, they did not file any return - Subsequently, on receipt of certain money by way of interest on enhanced compensation for acquisition of their agricultural land on 24-7-1989, assesses voluntarily filed returns of income for said assessment years on 18-5-1990 - Assessing Officer, though, accepted income so declared by assessees, but under section 139(8) for late filing of return and also under section 217 for not paying advance tax - Whether since by time assessees had received interest money from Government, period prescribed for filing return under section 139(4) for relevant assessment years was over and in those circumstances, charging of interest was not valid - Held, yes - Whether since prior to receipt of money, assessees could not have anticipated same, and hence, charging of interest under section 217 was also not valid - Held, yes

Section  149,  read with sections  147  and  148, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 / Section  282,  read with sections  279  and  280  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 – Income escaping assessment – Time limit for issuance of notice (Illustrations) - Assessment year  2013-14  - Assessee filed its return of income for Assessment year  2013-14  declaring NIL income after set-off of brought-forward loss - Case was selected for scrutiny and assessment under section 143(3) was completed determining total income of about Rs.10.62 lakhs - Assessee’s ledger reflected entries with three alleged entities: Acute Consultancy Ltd. showing a Rs.20 lakhs debit as opening balance; Sampada Chemicals Ltd. showing Rs.25 lakhs debit and a matching Rs.25 lakhs credit during year (net NIL); and Shyam Alcohol & Chemicals Ltd. showing a Rs.25 lakhs debit as opening balance - Pursuant to a search under section 132 in case of one 'V' in 2016 and alleged material on bogus accommodation entries, Assessing Officer issued a show-cause notice under section 148A(b) in May 2022 alleging that Rs.70 lakhs had entered assessee’s books from unexplained sources - Assessing Officer rejected objections by an order under section 148A(d) in July 2022 and issued a notice under section 148, proceeding on basis that entire Rs.70 lakhs constituted escaped income without giving effect to Rs.25 lakhs credit with Sampada Chemicals Ltd. - Whether since assessee’s ledger/credit entries were already on record, and on correct consideration alleged escaped income would fall below Rs.50,00,000, impugned reopening was barred by limitation under section 149 - Held, yes [Paras 9 and 10] [In favour of assessee]

Section 153, read with section 271(1)(c), of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Assessment - Time-limit for completion of - Assessment year 1985-86 - Whether where Assessing Officer had not recorded his opinion that case under consideration was falling under section 271(1)(c), mere issuing of notice under section 271(1)(c) was not sufficient to bring case within purview of section 153(1)(b) and no extended period of limitation of 8 years would be available to revenue authorities for completion of assessment - Held, yes

I. Section 145 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Method of accounting - System of accounting (Project Completion Method) - Assessment year 2016-17 - Assessee-firm was formed to carry on business of real estate development - Assessee was following ‘Project Completion Method’ - A search action under section 132 was conducted upon two doctors and it was found that they had paid cash of Rs. 11.20 crores to assessee in consideration for purchase of part of commercial building, out of which, Rs. 1 crore was found to have been paid during assessment year 2016-17 - Assessing Officer accordingly made addition of Rs. 1 crore to assessee's income for assessment year 2016-17 - It was noted that project in question, was completed in assessment year 2019-20 and that assessee had duly accounted and offered to tax cash receipts from two doctors by way of revenues in assessment year 2019-20 and that same had also been accepted and assessed to tax - Whether impugned sum was in nature of advance and, therefore, could not be taxed in relevant assessment year 2016-17 but, only in year in which project was completed i.e assessment year 2019-20 as assessee was following ‘Project Completion Method’ - Held, yes [Paras 7 and 8] [In favour of assessee]II. Section 68 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Cash Credit (Illustrations) - Assessment year 2016-17 - Assessee-firm was formed to carry on business of real estate development - Assessing Officer observed that, one MS in his statement, had averred that he along with one RS had paid Rs. 944.14 lakhs by way of demand-drafts towards purchase of share in assessee’s mall from 2012 and onwards - However, MS had admitted to payment of Rs.944.14 lakhs, out of which only Rs. 459.55 lakhs was found to be by way of cheque payment disclosed in books of accounts, difference of Rs.484.59 lakhs [Rs. 944.14 lakhs - Rs. 459.55 lakhs] could not be explained by MS - Assessing Officer treated difference as unaccounted receipt of assessee and added it to total income - It was noted that identical corresponding addition was also made by Assessing Officer of both doctors in their respective assessments on basis of statement of MS, which action of Assessing Officer was carried in appeal before First Appellate Authority, who was pleased to delete additions in hands of both MS and RS - Tribunal also upheld such deletion made by First Appellate Authority - Whether when addition on account of unexplained payments had been deleted in hands of purchasers, then consequential corresponding addition made by Assessing Officer in hands of assessee-seller had no legs to stand on - Held, yes - Whether, further, Assessing Officer relied on statements of two purchasers to saddle addition in hands of assessee, without giving a copy of same to assessee, thus, in absence of providing statements recorded during investigation, addition based solely on such statements could not be sustained - Held, yes [Paras 11 and 12][In favour of assessee]III. Section 36(1)(iii) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Interest on borrowed capital (Illustrations) - Assessment year 2016-17 - Whether where assessee’s own capital was far in excess of interest-free advances of lesser amount, it was to be presumed that interest-free advances were made out of own funds and not borrowings of assessee, thus, Commissioner (A) had rightly deleted impugned disallowance of interest by Assessing Officer - Held, yes [Paras 15 and 16] [In favour of assessee]IV. Section 22 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income from house property - Chargeable as (Unsold flats) - Assessment year 2017-18 - Whether annual letting value (ALV) of unsold flats is to be taxed - Held, yes - Whether Assessing Officer was correct in applying section 22 and adding deemed rent for unsold properties of assessee lying in closing stock of assessee - Held, yes [Para 22] [In favour of revenue]V. Section 40(a)(ia), read with section 194A, of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Business disallowance - Interest, etc., paid to a resident without deduction of tax at source (Illustration) - Assessment year 2017-18 - During year, assessee paid interest to a company on borrowed funds - No TDS was deducted on said interest payment under section 194A - Assessing Officer, thus, disallowed 30 per cent of expenditure under section 40(a)(ia) - Assessee claimed that payee was a regular income-tax filer who had included interest income in their income-tax return and paid taxes thereon, and therefore there could be no disallowance under section 40(a)(ia) - However, assessee was unable to furnish any evidence or requisite form to substantiate this claim - Whether, therefore, it would be fit to set aside issue back to file of Assessing Officer to verify whether payee had included interest income received from assessee, in their return of income and paid taxes thereon - Held, yes [Para 29] [Matter remanded]VI. Section 68 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Cash credit (Interest) - Assessment year 2017-18 - Assessee filed its return of income which was accepted and an assessment order was passed - During assessment year 2017-18, Assessing Officer noted that a liability of Rs. 15 lakhs was reflected in balance sheet by way of interest free security deposit received for leasing property for a hotel business - He was of view that assessee was unable to substantiate low rent received or genuineness of deposit and therefore, added outstanding liability by way of unexplained cash credit under section 68 - Assessee contended that impugned sum had been received and credited in books from tenant long back and that amount represented opening balance of liability brought forward from earlier years - Whether rigors of section 68 can be applied only to sums found credited in books of accounts in that particular year, and not those which were credited in earlier years - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, lower authorities had erred in invoking and applying provisions of section 68 to opening balance of liabilities brought forward from earlier years - Held, yes [Para 31] [In favour of assessee]VII. Section 145, read with section 43CB of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Method of accounting - Change of (project completion method) - Assessment year 2017-18 - Assessee-firm was engaged in business of real estate development - Since inception of its business, assessee had been consistently and regularly following project completion method of accounting - Assessing Officer opined that as per section 43CB, which was applicable in relevant assessment year 2017-18, assessee was statutorily required to disclose income from its projects under percentage completion method - Accordingly, he re-computed income of assessee from real estate project by applying percentage completion method and made addition to income of assessee - It was noted that projects of assessee were commenced much prior to 1-4-2016 and having regard to transitional provisions of ICDS-III, revenue from same should be recognized based on project completion method which was regularly followed by assessee prior to previous year beginning from 1-4-2016 - Whether therefore, Assessing Officer was unjustified in changing and applying percentage completion method - Held, yes - Whether, further, provisions of section 43CB read with ICDS-III are applicable to contractors and not developers and therefore, assessee being a developer was under no obligation to apply percentage completion method - Held, yes [Paras 38 to 41] [In favour of assessee]  Circulars and Notifications : Circular No. 10/2017 dated 23.03.2017

Section  2(47),  read with section  45,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961/ Section  2(109),  read with section  67,  of the Income-tax Act, 2025 -  Capital gains  -  Transfer  (Scope of) - Assessment year  2017-18  -Assessee purchased 37 bighas of land in Himachal Pradesh, financed largely by M/s Homeland Buildwell Pvt. Ltd. (HBPL) -Collaboration agreement entered into in 2006 for joint development could not materialize owing to restrictions under State law and amount received from HBPL was treated as unsecured loan - Assessee developed mall on part of land and remaining land was held as fixed asset - During relevant previous year, assessee transferred 16.5 bighas to HBPL in execution of arbitral award towards discharge of outstanding loan liability and declared long-term capital gain of Rs. 91,738 - Assessing Officer held that transfer had taken place in financial year 2006-07 and, therefore, capital gains were not taxable in assessment year under consideration and made addition of Rs. 2.42 crores -Commissioner (Appeals) deleted addition - It was noted that revenue had accepted assessee’s ownership of land and loan from HBPL in prior years, and land was in assessee’s exclusive possession until transferred in financial yer 2016-17 to satisfy arbitral decree - Whether since in order to satisfy arbitral decree, assessee had transferred land and loan liability was eliminated, it was to be construed as price of land received by assessee in relevant year i.e. 2017-18 year - Held,yes - Whether therefore, capital gains were chargeable in assessment year 2017-18 and addition was liable to be deleted - Held,yes [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]

Section 5 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual of - Assessment year 1983-84 - IAC brought to tax process escalation amount of Rs. 466.92 lakhs in assessment year 1982-83 by virtue of interim relief granted by Delhi High Court and observed that if Supreme Court reversed order of Delhi High Court, assessee could claim liability arising out of Supreme Court’s order in year in which latter passed its order - Whether IAC was correct to say so, since Supreme Court’s order did not create a liability but only determined and quantified assessee’s claim - Held, no

Section 5 ,  read with section 271(1)(c) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Accrual of - Assessment year 1988-89 - Assessing Officer brought interest on enhanced compensation received by assessee to tax on receipt basis in assessment year 1988-89 and thereafter, also imposed penalty upon assessee under section 271(1)(c) - Whether since interest in instant case related to period 10-11-1976 to 9-12-1986 and assessee was not in receipt of any interest for assessment year 1988-89, same could not be brought to tax in said year and was liable to be spread over among years to which it pertained - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, impugned penalty was also liable to be deleted - Held, yes

II.Section 4  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Income - Chargeable as (Deposits) - Assessment years 2004-05 to 2008-09 - Assessee-club received advance membership fee for 25 years from its members towards enjoyment of various facilities provided by it - Assessee's case was that there was a contractual obligation on it to appropriate said advance membership fees over tenure of membership and same could not be brought to tax in its entirety in year of receipt - Assessing Officer rejected assessee's plea and brought entire receipt of advance membership fee to tax in year of receipt itself - Whether since assessee had received advance membership fee for 25 years, concept of matching principles was to be applied while computing income under Act and entire amount received by assessee could not be brought to tax in year of receipt itself - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, impugned order was to be set aside and, matter was to be remanded back to work out spread/rollover of advance membership fee collected for a period of 25 years on basis of a reasonable scientific method - Held, yes [Para 8] [In favour of assessee/Matter remanded]

Section 73 of the Finance Act, 1994 - Recovery of service tax not levied or paid or short-levied or short-paid or erroneously refunded - Period February 2000 to January 2004 - Assessee was an air travel booking agent - Show-cause notice dated 15-7-2005 was issued to it demanding service tax for relevant period - Assessee challenged said demand contending that demand could not be enforced beyond 5 years; that service tax was payable after receipt of same from dealers; therefore, question of payment of service tax in advance did not arise when certain amount was due from dealers which was not received; and that it was entitled to cum-tax benefit - Adjudicating authority as well as Commissioner (Appeals) without considering above pleas of assessee confirmed demand on assessee - Whether matter was to be remanded to original authority for de novo consideration - Held, yes [Para 3]

Section 65 of the Finance Act, 1994 - Club or association service - Period 16-6-2005 to 30-9-2006 - Stay Order - Appellants were running holiday resorts in various parts of country - They collected amount from individuals/partnership firms/companies who were admitted as ‘time sharers’, otherwise called ‘members’ - Authorities below taking view that appellants were covered under category of ‘Club or association service’ under section 65(25a) confirmed demand of service tax of over Rs. 2.5 crores against them under proviso to section 73(1) - On instant appeal, it was submitted that on terms and conditions of agreement entered into between appellants and a time-sharer, latter received a right to stay in former’s holiday resorts and avail of various facilities, amenities and advantages for prescribed period and he could enjoy benefit under a certificate of membership known as ‘Trump Certificate’ - Appellants contended that as Trump Certificate was freely transferable for a determinate value by a member to any other person at any stage, it qualified to be ‘goods’ within meaning of this word defined under Sale of Goods Act - An alternate argument was that Trump Certificate should be regarded as a deed of conveyance of a right to reside in immovable property; that a major part of amounts paid by certificate-holder to appellants was in nature of rental for such right to reside in resort; that such amount was not exigible to levy of service tax prior to 1-7-2007; and that, for period of dispute, appellants were not liable to pay any service-tax in respect of aforesaid amount - Appellants further pleaded limitation against impugned demand contending that taxable service in question was introduced only with effect from 16-6-2005 and, therefore, appellants could not be held to have suppressed any fact material to that service before department prior to said date; it was, accordingly, argued that extended period of limitation was not invocable in instant case - Whether prima facie, each holiday resort run by appellants answered definition of ‘club’ or ‘association’ given under section 65(25a) - Held, yes - Whether, in said view of matter, appellants could not be said to have made out a prima facie case against impugned demand of service tax on merits - Held, yes - Whether, in such a situation, plea of ‘goods’ and alternate plea of ‘immovable property’ would not be sustainable - Held, yes - Whether, however, on an overall assessment of case including plea of limitation, appellants were to be directed to pre-deposit only a part of amount of service tax covered by impugned order - Held, yes (Stay granted)

facts.text:
The assessee was a hotelier but had not done any hotel business as it completed the construction of the hotel during the previous year corresponding to the assessment year 1985-86. In response to notice under section 148 a loss of Rs. 1,20,097 was declared in the return. The entire dispute was regarding the cost of construction of the hotel. The assessee maintained regular books of account which showed the total cost at Rs. 13,58,193. The Assessing Officer referred the matter to the DVO, who determined the cost at Rs. 19,89,000. The assessee also got the property valued by a registered valuer who determined the total cost at Rs. 16,80,906. Ultimately, the difference between the cost of construction determined by the DVO and shown by the assessee, i.e., Rs. 6,30,807, was subjected to tax by the Assessing Officer as unexplained investment under section 69B. On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) adopted the cost determined by the registered valuer. After adding for extra items and electricity and giving an allowance of 10 per cent for self-supervision, he arrived at the cost of Rs. 16,38,900. Deducting from this, the cost shown by the assessee, he sustained an addition of Rs. 2,80,707. This was spread over the five assessment years commencing from 1981-82.

On cross-appeals:

The ITO disallowed certain amount under section 40A(8) claimed by the assessee-company for the assessment year 1976-77, corresponding to the accounting year ended on 30-6-1975. On appeal before the Commissioner (Appeals), the assessee challenged the disallowance under section 40A(8) on the ground that section 40A(8) having been introduced with effect from 1-4-1976 would be applicable to expenditure incurred on payment of interest on deposits from that date and not to interest paid prior to that date and as the assessee’s previous year relating to the assessment year 1976-77 ended on 30-6-1975, provisions of section 40A(8) were inapplieable to this year. The Commissioner (Appeals), however, rejected the assessee’s contention and upheld the ITO’s order.

On second appeal:

For the assessment years 1984-85 to 1986-87 the assessee failed to file the returns within the due time under section 14(1). In the course of search at his premises on 12-6-1986 it was noticed that the assessee concealed particulars in respect of his wealth and investment made in construction work. Notices under section 17 were served upon the assessee on 25-2-1988 for the years under consideration and in response the assessee filed the returns of net wealth on 31-3-1990 for all the Years. The Assessing Officer completed the assessments under section 16(3) on 22-2-1991 at a wealth little higher than that disclosed and imposed penalty under section 18(1)(c). The difference between the net wealth declared and net wealth assessed was on account of the fact that while valuing the properties, i.e., chawls and dwelling units, owned by the assessee, which were acquired in the earlier years and leased out to tenants, on rent capitalisation method, the Assessing Officer did not allow 6 per cent collection charges from the gross rent for working out the net maintainable rent for each year. On appeal, it was contended that neither Explanation 3 nor Explanations 4 and 5 to section 18(1)(c) were applicable to his case. The Commissioner (Appeals) rejected the assessee’s contention and confirmed the penalties levied by the Assessing Officer.

On second appeal, besides reiterating his earlier contentions, the assessee argued that Explanation 5 to section 18(1)(c) was not applicable to the instant case as this Explanation could be invoked only where on search the assessee was found to be the owner of unaccounted money, bullion, jewellery or other valuable articles or things and the same had not been disclosed in the returns already filed or no returns had been filed before the date of search; the term ‘valuable articles or things’ used in the Explanation refers only to movable assets which are capable of being in possession of the assessee and seizure by the department at the time of search whereas in the present case the wealth was mainly composed of immovable property which was in existence before the date of search and no search operations were required to search the same out within the meaning of section 132 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 or section 37A of the Wealth-tax Act. On the other hand, the revenue justified the levy of penalty on the plea that had there been no search the assessee would have succeeded in evading the due wealth-tax for the years under consideration and that the case was covered by Explanation 5 to section 18(1)(c).

The assessee owned a cinema theatre. The registered valuer had valued it as on 31-3-1982 at Rs. 54 lakhs. The registered valuer ascertained the value of the asset by adopting the land and building method. While arriving at the value he had taken the land value of 229.48 sq. mtrs. at the prevailing market rate of Rs. 300 per sq. mtrs. He had estimated the life of the asset at 80 years. The WTO did not agree with the valuation given to the asset for the assessment year 1982-83. He referred the question of valuation of the said asset to the valuation cell of the Income-tax Department Rejecting the assessee’s objections the Valuation Officer valued the cinema at Rs.72 lakhs by adopting the income capitalisation method. The WTO adopted the departmental valuer’s report and determined the value of the asset at Rs.72 lakhs. The Commissioner (Appeals) also confirmed the valuation made by the WTO.

On second appeal, the assessee contended that while arriving at the figure the Departmental Valuation Officer did not take into consideration several factors which should have been considered and the estimated net profit per year should have been proportionately reduced:

The assessee carried forward depreciation for a number of years - the earliest of which, was 1998-99. For assessment year 2010-11, the Assessing Officer disallowed the amounts claimed as depreciation on the ground that the amendment in section 32(2), which removed the cap, was prospective and effective only from 1-4-2002.

The Commissioner (Appeals), however, reversed said decision.

The Tribunal upheld, the decision of the Commissioner (Appeals).

The question came up for consideration was as to whether interpretation of section 32(2) as amended by Finance Act, 2001, could be given effect to beyond period of eight years, prior to its commencement?

On revenue's appeal:

The assessee, a financial corporation, was involved in long-term finance of infrastructural facilities. For the relevant assessment year, the assessee claimed deduction under section 36(1)(viii). The Assessing Officer disallowed the assessee’s claim.

On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) upheld the impugned order.

On appeal by the assessee, the revenue contended that the assessee had made representation only on March 28, 2000 seeking approval from the Central Board of Direct Taxes, in fact the assessment year was 1999-2000, such request for approval was not made to the concerned authorities at the earlier stage, and that the amendment to section 36(1)(viii) was with effect from 1-4-2000 and that the same could not have retrospective effect.

The land for the assessee-hotel was provided by a HUF whereas the building was constructed by one D who was an individual. The said HUF and the individual had entered into an agreement to form and promote the assessee-company. By a resolution, the Board of directors of the assessee approved the total expenditure incurred by D and directed that the same be incorporated in the books of the assessee for the year ended 30-6-1976 by crediting to the account of D. In its return for the assessment year 1977-78 the assessee disclosed the amount spent on the construction of the building.

In the assessment proceedings of D for the assessment years 1975-76 to 1977-78, the ITO refused to accept the figure disclosed by the said individual as the amount spent on construction. On the basis of the opinion of the Valuation Officer, the ITO was of the opinion that the total amount spent on construction was Rs. 14,11,485 and not Rs. 10,04,292 as claimed by D. He, accordingly, sought to add the difference to the income of D for the aforesaid years. D challenged the same by way of appeal and the matter was ultimately carried to the Tribunal. The Tribunal held that the said additions could not be made to the income of D and that he could not be asked to explain the source of the said investment. It observed that the assessee was responsible for explaining the source of investment in such construction.

On the basis of the above findings, a notice was given to the assessee proposing to reopen its assessment for the assessment year 1977-78. On writ petition against the notice the assessee contended (i) that the notice did not satisfy the requirements of section 151 of the Act as section 151 requires not only the approval of the Board but also the approval of the Commissioner where a notice under section 147/148 is issued after the expiry of eight years; (ii) that section 147(b) was not attracted in the present case and, therefore, it could not be invoked by the assessing authority against the petitioner; (iii) that the jurisdictional facts necessary to invoke the power under section 147(a) were not present in this case and, hence, the notice was invalid.

The Assessing Officer noted that assessee had earned tax free dividend income and he required the assessee to explain as to why disallowance under rule 8D should not be made. Assessee submitted that in order to pay 'upfront fee' of Rs. 150 crores to AAI, assessee had approached banks for such a payment and since funding by way of borrowing of such payment was taking time it was decided to bring equity and the surplus arising from the operation was kept in mutual funds. When the funding was received, then the same got substituted by the borrowed money of Rs. 150 crores from the banks which was utilised in incurring of cost of airport project. Thus, investment in funds was not made from borrowed funds but from share capital and internal accruals from time to time.

However, the Assessing Officer applied the provision of rule 8D for making the disallowance.

The Commissioner (Appeals) held that same could not be disallowed, because assessee had owned interest free funds sufficient to cover the investment made and therefore, no apportionment of any interest expenses could be made for the purpose of disallowance under section 14A. He further held that provision of rule 8D were not applicable in assessment year 2007-08 as the same had been made applicable for the assessment year 2008-09.

On appeal:

The assessee-company was in the business of selling timeshare units in its various resorts. During relevant assessment years, the assessee collected revenue from timeshare members but same was not recognised as revenue for the current year. The explanation of the assessee was that it had considered only 40 per cent of the membership fees collected as income and the balance 60 per cent was treated as deferred income. It was stated that the balance amount was to be spread over the next 33 years during which the assessee was expected to provide timeshare facilities to the members. It was also stated that in order to provide various facilities during the next 33 years, it had to incur many costs. Further explanation of the assessee was that the AMC was exclusively meant to cover the maintenance of various facilities which were an integral part of the timeshare property. These charges were for the maintenance of various electronic gadgets made available in the accommodation, furniture, kitchen equipments, central air-conditioning etc. On the other hand, the consideration for future obligations received in the initial stages was towards transfer facility from one resort to another, split, accumulation and advancing facility, domestic and international exchange, transmission, upgradation etc. The Assessing Officer observed that the assessee was following mercantile system of accounting and, hence, income had to be accounted for on accrual basis. He was of the view that the receipt was undisputedly income as the assessee itself had shown it as deferred income. However, the Act does not recognise the concept of deferred income and, hence, the assessee’s explanation could not be accepted.
